title: Submission Instructions
summary: Submission link, review rules, page limits, and formatting instructions for IEEE SSCI 2027.

sections.heading: Submission Link
paragraphs: Full and short paper submissions should be made through the IEEE SSCI 2027 online submission system. The submission link will be added when the submission site opens.
The deadline for full and short paper submissions is 10 August 2026.
Submissions for late breaking papers, abstract poster-only presentations, and journal-to-conference presentation submissions are also welcome.

sections.heading: Paper Submission Rules and Guidelines
bullets: Each paper should not reveal author identities during the double-anonymous review process.

All authors must have contributed significantly to the paper at the time of submission. By submitting to IEEE SSCI 2027, authors acknowledge that they conform to IEEE authorship and submission policies.

The use of artificial intelligence generated text in an article must be disclosed in the acknowledgements section of any paper submitted to an IEEE conference or periodical. The sections of the paper that use AI-generated text must cite the AI system used to generate the text.
No authorship changes will be allowed after acceptance.
All papers must respect the paper formatting rules. Alterations of spacing, font size, margins, or other changes that deviate from the template may result in desk rejection without further review.

Full papers, short papers, and late breaking papers must be original, not previously published elsewhere, and not under review or submitted for review elsewhere while under consideration for IEEE SSCI 2027.

Abstract poster-only submissions and journal-to-conference papers must not have been previously presented, under consideration for presentation, or submitted for presentation at other conferences, congresses, symposia, or workshops while under consideration for presentation at IEEE SSCI 2027.
Journal-to-conference papers must have been accepted at IEEE Transactions journals sponsored by CIS and first appeared in IEEE Xplore within the past 2 years.

Papers will be checked for plagiarism. The Program Committee reserves the right to desk-reject a paper if it contains elements suspected to be plagiarized. Program chairs may share submission lists with chairs of other conferences with overlapping review periods and may use external plagiarism detection software.
Authors must respect the page limitation for the respective paper type.
All papers must be submitted through the IEEE SSCI 2027 online submission system.
For full or short papers, please add a statement about data/code sharing following the open science instructions below.

For an accepted full paper to be included in the symposium program, the proceedings, and IEEE Xplore, the final accepted paper must be submitted by the final version deadline, the corresponding registration fees must be paid by the required registration deadline, and the paper must be presented by at least one author at the conference.

sections.heading: Page Limitation and Submission Format
paragraphs: All papers must be submitted using the IEEE conference proceedings template with body text in 10-point type. LaTeX users must use \documentclass[10pt,conference]{IEEEtran}.
The page limitations are as follows:
bullets: Full papers: up to 6 pages, plus 1 page for references. A maximum of two extra content pages per full paper is allowed, up to 8 pages plus 1 page for references, with an additional charge per extra page.
Short papers: up to 4 pages, plus 1 page for references.
Late breaking papers: extended abstracts of up to 2 pages, including references, if any.
Abstract poster-only submissions: up to 250 words.
Journal to conference submissions: up to 1 page listing bullet points with the highlights of the paper and explaining why the paper is relevant to SSCI.

paragraphs: For a description of each paper type, please refer to the call for papers.

sections.heading: Open Science for Full and Short Papers
paragraphs: Authors of full and short papers are encouraged to make data and code available upon acceptance to increase reproducibility and replicability.

Please add a note in the last paragraph of the introduction of your submitted paper either stating that you will make your data/code available upon acceptance or explaining why you cannot make your data/code available. Replace this note with a link to the data/code in the final version if you are sharing materials. You may use any online repository for this purpose.
